name: Minnesota
tagline: North Shore cliffs, Iron Range pine and the Mississippi from its first trickle to the bluffs at Winona.
intro: Minnesota's byways follow Lake Superior up the North Shore, run back into the pine and lake country of the Chippewa and Superior national forests, and trace the Mississippi, the Minnesota and the St. Croix through prairie farms and river towns. This chapter follows the Minnesota Scenic Byways program, run by the Minnesota Department of Transportation with Explore Minnesota; most member pages link to the byway's own organization or its Explore Minnesota profile.

members.name: Apple Blossom Drive Scenic Byway
members.blurb: County Highway 29 leaves La Crescent for the bluff tops, past orchards and roadside cider stands, with the Mississippi valley spread below the overlooks at Great River Bluffs State Park.

members.name: Avenue of Pines Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 46 runs northwest from Deer River to Northome through stands of mature red pine, opening now and then onto marsh and the wide water of Lake Winnibigoshish and Cut Foot Sioux.

members.name: Edge of the Wilderness National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 38 runs north from Grand Rapids to Effie over the rolling hills of the Chippewa National Forest, past bogs and fishing lakes, on a line once traveled by voyageurs and loggers.

members.name: Glacial Ridge Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Loops of country road wander between Willmar and Glenwood over hills and ridges left by melting glaciers, past lakes set among the farm fields and into the prairie and hardwood of Sibley and Glacial Lakes state parks.

members.name: Grand Rounds National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A ring of city parkways first imagined by Horace Cleveland circles Minneapolis, passing the Chain of Lakes and the waterfall in Minnehaha Park on its way to the old Stone Arch Bridge on the Mississippi.

members.name: Great River Road All-American Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Great River Road follows the Mississippi 565 miles from a stream you can step across at Itasca, past Paul Bunyan and Babe in Bemidji, down to river towns under wooded bluffs at Red Wing and Winona.

members.name: Gunflint Trail National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: County Road 12 runs 57 miles inland from the harbor at Grand Marais through pine and birch, on an old footpath named for the spark-striking chert French explorers found at Gunflint Lake.

members.name: Historic Bluff Country National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 16 follows the Root River valley between La Crescent and Dexter under wooded dolomite bluffs, through pasture and trout-stream country where an Amish buggy on the road is an ordinary sight.

members.name: Historic Highway 75 "King of Trails"
members.blurb: US 75 runs the length of Minnesota near its western border, from the Iowa line to Canada through prairie and farm country, on a road known as the King of Trails before the state numbered its highways.

members.name: Lady Slipper Scenic Byway
members.blurb: County Road 39 runs 28 miles from Blackduck to US 2 through the Chippewa National Forest, crossing the Mississippi and passing the old barracks of the Rabideau CCC camp, with lady slippers in bloom by late June.

members.name: Lake Country Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 34 crosses from prairie to pine between Detroit Lakes and Walker, past lakes where people have summered at resorts for generations, with a spur north from Park Rapids to the Mississippi headwaters at Itasca State Park.

members.name: Lake Mille Lacs Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 68-mile loop rings Lake Mille Lacs through Garrison, Isle and Onamia, past the Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post at Vineland. In winter the lake becomes more than 130,000 acres of ice for fishing and kiteboarding.
members.note: Route line from MnDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Minnesota River Valley National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Roads follow the Minnesota River 300 miles from Big Stone Lake down to Belle Plaine, through farm country and river towns like New Ulm, past Fort Ridgely and the Lower Sioux Agency, places marked by the U.S.-Dakota War of 1862.

members.name: North Shore All-American Scenic Drive
members.blurb: Old 61 and then Highway 61 follow Lake Superior 154 miles from Duluth to Grand Portage, through Two Harbors and Grand Marais and past the Split Rock lighthouse, first lit in 1910 on a 133-foot cliff.

members.name: Otter Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 150-mile loop through Otter Tail County links Fergus Falls, Perham and Battle Lake among more than a thousand lakes, with a long view from Inspiration Peak and the 1889 Phelps Mill on the Otter Tail River.

members.name: Paul Bunyan National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: County roads loop twice through pine and lake country between Pequot Lakes and Crosslake, in a district whose lakes are said to be Paul Bunyan's footprints and where the Pequot Lakes water tower is painted as his fishing bobber.

members.name: Saint Croix Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Point Douglas near Hastings the byway follows the St. Croix valley 124 miles north, from long views over rolling ground into rocky, wooded country along one of the original wild and scenic rivers.

members.name: Shooting Star Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 56 runs about 30 miles from I-90 to the Iowa line through Adams and Le Roy, one of the state's first wildflower routes, its roadsides kept in native grasses and the flowers that bloom there in June and July.

members.name: Skyline Drive
members.blurb: Skyline Parkway traces the old beach line of Glacial Lake Duluth along the hills above the city, looking down on the harbor and the St. Louis River bay, and ends at Hawk Ridge, a lookout for migrating birds.
members.note: MnDOT lists it as Skyline Drive; the City of Duluth calls the road Skyline Parkway.

members.name: Superior National Forest Scenic Byway
members.blurb: County roads cross 78 miles of the Superior National Forest from the Iron Range at Aurora and Hoyt Lakes to Silver Bay on Lake Superior, passing the Toimi School, a one-room Finnish schoolhouse from 1913.

members.name: Veterans Evergreen Memorial Drive
members.blurb: Highway 23, long called the scenic route to Duluth, runs 50 miles from near Banning State Park through Askov and Wrenshall, over trout streams, to a veterans' overlook above the St. Louis River valley.

members.name: Waters of the Dancing Sky Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 11 runs west from International Falls close to the Canadian border, following the Rainy River to Baudette and skirting Lake of the Woods, under northern lights frequent enough to name the byway.
